key_insight: Training LLMs to reason about security detections, not just predict a label, improves triage quality and makes automated decisions more reliable when paired with a separate confidence calibrator.
engineering_relevance: For SOC automation, this approach can reduce alert fatigue while preserving high-confidence handling of benign and malicious endpoint detections.
method: Train a chain-of-thought triage classifier on human-labeled Windows endpoint detections.
Use automated prompt optimization, self-training, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
Add a separate calibrator that reads the full reasoning trace to estimate verdict correctness.
evidence_signal: The system reports 82.6% test accuracy and, at the high-confidence automated-triage setting, improves benign recall by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% over a direct-label LLM classifier.
watch_item: Reasoning can degrade label-token probabilities, so automated triage needs a trained calibrator; an untrained confidence judge collapses high-confidence recall to zero.
paper_title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models
